pr_title: feat(assets): allow `new URL` to resolve package assets
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing! -->

### Description

<!-- Please insert your description here and provide especially info about the "what" this PR is solving -->
This change allows modules to resolve asset URLs for assets located underneath a package path. E.g. `new URL('@scope/component/assets/logo.png', import.meta.url)`

close #6918 

### Additional context

<!-- e.g. is there anything you'd like reviewers to focus on? -->
I Implemented this in a backwards-compatible way by using a resolver which prefers relative paths and makes the root path resolve to the public base path.

---

Thanks for your PR. But I'm not sure if this is necessary, because the type of new URL is 

```ts
constructor (input: string, base?: string | URL);
```

Maybe `new URL('@/hello.js')` or `new URL('/hello.js')` are better. But I'm not sure if there will be boundary conditions in this expression.

review_comments:
GitHub doesn't allow me to highlight line41:

```js
const rawUrl = code.slice(urlStart, urlEnd)
```

In development mode if `rawUrl` starts with a `.`, I think we can `continue` the while loop, as we leave the code as is for the browser to resolve like the current Vite behaviour.

That makes sense. I was also wondering if it makes sense for us to turn off `preferRelative: true` in the resolver. I decided not to since I believe it's unintuitive for `new URL("./foo.png", import.meta.url)` to have different behavior `new URL("foo.png", import.meta.url)`.
Yeah we can leave `preferRelative: true` as is so it's consistent with the glob behaviour.
I don't know why here need to `new URL(${JSON.stringify(builtUrl)}, self.location)`, thank you very much if you could tell me

Really I just added this for consistency with the asset loader. The only edge case I can think of where this might have an effect is when the page has a `<base href="https://some-external-origin.com">` tag. Including `self.location` ensures that the asset/worker with a relative public path is resolved relative to the current origin instead of wherever the `<base>` tag is referencing. Given that Vite is the one responsible for rendering the index page, this behavior seems appropriate.
